course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Global Conflict
unit.description: Study how empires collapsed, why two world wars were fought and how they were conducted, how the Depression reshaped economies, and how mass atrocities happened.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was a feature of fascism?
choices: Support for free elections and competition among many parties
Belief in international communism
Support for democracy and a strong leader
Rejection of democracy and obedience to one leader
questions.explanation: Fascism demanded obedience to a single leader and rejected democracy.
choiceExplanations: Fascists wanted a single leader, not elections.
Fascism demanded obedience to a single leader and rejected democracy.

questions.prompt: At the Munich conference in 1938, Britain and France
choices: allowed Germany to take the Sudetenland
declared war on Germany
forced Germany to leave Austria
allowed Germany to take Poland
questions.explanation: They agreed to let Germany take the Sudetenland.
choiceExplanations: They agreed to let Germany take the Sudetenland.
Poland was invaded in 1939, which led to war.
questions.distinguisher: The Munich agreement concerned Czechoslovakia's Sudetenland, not Poland.

questions.prompt: Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor is best explained by
choices: Japan's alliance with the United States
the US oil sales that Japan wished to expand into a formal alliance
the US oil embargo and Japan's plan to seize Southeast Asia
a US invasion of Japan in 1940
questions.explanation: After the oil embargo, Japan planned to seize resource-rich colonies and attacked the US fleet.

The US had cut off oil.
After the oil embargo, Japan planned to seize resource-rich colonies and attacked the US fleet.
questions.distinguisher: The US had cut off oil sales; Japan was not trying to expand them.

questions.prompt: Which of the following helped the Nazi Party gain support?
choices: Economic prosperity and full employment in Germany in the early 1930s

Economic crisis and resentment of the treaty boosted the Nazis.
questions.distinguisher: Germany was in depression, not prosperity, in the early 1930s.

questions.prompt: Which claim about the causes of World War II is most defensible?
choices: The war was caused only by events in Asia
Unchecked aggression in Europe and Asia led to a global war
The war began only when Germany invaded Poland in September 1939
Appeasement stopped Hitler's expansion
questions.explanation: German, Italian, and Japanese expansion together produced global war.
choiceExplanations: German, Italian, and Japanese expansion together produced global war.
questions.distinguisher: Japan's war in China began in 1937, before the invasion of Poland.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.6 key concept: the causes of World War II included the rise of fascist and totalitarian regimes that used violence and propaganda and pursued expansion
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the rise of fascism, 1919–1939
stimulusBlocks.text:
Fascism glorified the nation, rejected democracy and communism, and demanded obedience to a single leader. Benito Mussolini took power in Italy in 1922. In Germany, the Depression and resentment of the Versailles treaty helped Adolf Hitler's Nazi Party grow, and Hitler became chancellor in 1933.

The Nazis quickly destroyed democracy, banned other parties, and persecuted Jews. Both regimes used propaganda and violence to control society and promised to restore national greatness through expansion.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which helped Hitler's party grow?
choices: Support from the Soviet Union
The Depression and resentment of Versailles
Germany's victory over France and Russia in World War I
Prosperity in the 1920s
questions.explanation: The passage names the Depression and resentment of the treaty.
choiceExplanations: The Nazis were hostile to Soviet communism in the 1930s.
The passage names the Depression and resentment of the treaty.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, Britain and France pursued appeasement because they
choices: wanted to help Germany expand eastward against the Soviet Union
had defeated Germany in 1938
were allied with the Soviet Union
were scarred by World War I and wanted to avoid war
questions.explanation: They were scarred by World War I and hoped to avoid another war.
choiceExplanations: Germany signed a pact with the Soviets.
They were scarred by World War I and hoped to avoid another war.
questions.distinguisher: They hoped to avoid war, not to help Germany.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.6 key concept: the failure of the Paris peace settlement and the policy of appeasement contributed to the outbreak of World War II
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing appeasement and the outbreak of war in Europe, 1936–1939
stimulusBlocks.text:
Hitler rearmed Germany in violation of the Versailles treaty and annexed Austria in 1938. Britain and France, still scarred by World War I, tried to avoid another war through appeasement. At Munich in September 1938, they agreed to let Germany take the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia.

In August 1939, Germany and the Soviet Union signed a pact not to attack each other. On September 1, 1939, Germany invaded Poland, and Britain and France declared war.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, the immediate cause of war between Britain and Germany was
choices: Germany's invasion of Poland
Germany's annexation of Austria
Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor
the Munich agreement
questions.explanation: Britain and France declared war after Germany invaded Poland.
choiceExplanations: Britain and France declared war after Germany invaded Poland.
Munich was an attempt to avoid war.
questions.distinguisher: The annexation of Austria in 1938 did not lead to war.

In August 1939, Germany and the Soviet Union signed a pact not to attack each other. On September 1, 1939, Germany invaded Poland, and Britain and France declared war.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, Japan seized Manchuria in 1931 mainly to gain
choices: a naval base in Hawaii
an alliance with China
raw materials and markets
democratic reforms
questions.explanation: The passage says Japan sought raw materials and markets.
choiceExplanations: Hawaii is not mentioned in this context.
The passage says Japan sought raw materials and markets.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.6 key concept: Japanese imperial expansion in Asia was a cause of World War II
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing Japanese expansion, 1931–1941
stimulusBlocks.text:
Seeking raw materials and markets during the Depression, Japanese army officers seized Manchuria in northeastern China in 1931. Japan launched a full-scale war against China in 1937; when Japanese troops captured Nanjing, they killed many thousands of civilians and prisoners.

When the United States cut off oil exports to Japan in 1941, Japanese leaders decided to seize the resource-rich colonies of Southeast Asia. On December 7, 1941, Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, the US oil embargo led Japanese leaders to
choices: withdraw from China
ally with the United States
end the war in China
plan to seize Southeast Asian colonies
questions.explanation: Japan decided to seize resource-rich colonies.
choiceExplanations: Japan decided to seize resource-rich colonies.
questions.distinguisher: Japan did not withdraw from China.

questions.prompt: Japan's seizure of Manchuria in 1931 is best understood in the context of
choices: the prosperity of the 1920s and rising world trade
the Great Depression and competition for resources
the end of World War II

questions.explanation: The passage links the seizure to the search for raw materials and markets during the Depression.

Japan was not allied with the Soviet Union.
questions.distinguisher: The seizure came as the Depression shrank trade, not during prosperity.
